title: Corporate Flight Bookings
description: Brute force to optimized: touching every flight in a range for every booking versus a difference array that marks only the two endpoints, reconstructed with one prefix-sum sweep.

blocks.text: Problem Summary: There are n flights, numbered 1 to n. Given a list of bookings, each [first, last, seats], meaning seats seats were reserved for every flight from first to last, inclusive, return an array of length n where the ith value is the total number of seats reserved on flight i plus 1 (using 0-based output indices).

blocks.caption: What goes in, what comes out

blocks.content: {"headers":["Aspect","Detail"],"rows":[["Input","n (number of flights), bookings (a list of [first, last, seats] triples, 1-indexed flights)"],["Output","The total seats reserved on each flight"],["Goal","Apply every booking without touching every flight in its range individually"],["Constraints","1 <= n <= 20000; 1 <= bookings.length <= 20000; 1 <= first <= last <= n"]]}

{"headers":["Signal in the problem","Pattern it points to"],"rows":[["Every booking adds the same seat count across an entire RANGE of flights","A difference array, exactly the same technique as Range Addition"],["The final seat counts are only needed once, after all bookings are applied","One final prefix-sum pass reconstructs every flight's total from the difference marks"]]}

blocks.text: This is the Range Addition problem in a flight-booking setting: start with n flights at 0 reserved seats, and for every booking, add its seat count to every flight from first to last, then report the final seat count on every flight.

blocks.title: Analogy: Tallying Seats Booked Across a Range of Flights
blocks.text: Picture a booking system where a travel agency reserves the same number of seats across a consecutive range of flights in one transaction. Instead of updating every flight in that range individually, marking just where the reservation starts and ends, then tallying once at the end, is far faster.

blocks.caption: Mark the start and just-past-the-end of each booking; a running sum tallies every flight

blocks.text: Flight 1 only gets the first booking's 10 seats; flight 2 gets all three bookings, 10 + 20 + 25 = 55; and so on, giving [10, 55, 45, 25, 25].
Flight 1 gets 10 seats; flight 2 gets the first booking's 10 plus the second booking's 15, giving [10, 25].
This problem is structurally identical to Range Addition: a range update (a booking) needs to be applied efficiently, and only the final result, after every booking, is ever needed.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: Reserving seats seats on every flight from first to last is the same as saying "the running reservation total increases by seats starting at first, and decreases back by seats right after last."

Observation 2: Recording just those two marks per booking, in a difference array, takes O(1) per booking instead of O(range length).

Observation 3: A single left-to-right running sum over the difference array, after every booking has been marked, reconstructs the exact total on every flight.

Observation 4: This is exactly the difference array technique used for Range Addition, applied here to flights and seat counts instead of an abstract array and increments.
This leads directly to marking only the two endpoints of each booking in a difference array, then reconstructing every flight's total with a single prefix-sum sweep.
For every booking, walk through its entire flight range directly, adding its seat count to each flight.

items: Initialize an array of n flights, all starting at 0 reserved seats.
For every booking [first, last, seats], add seats to every flight from first to last (converting to 0-based indices).
Return the array after every booking has been applied.

blocks.caption: Brute force flow: touch every flight in a range, for every booking

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: Every booking is applied fully and immediately across its entire range.
The array reflects a completely up-to-date state after each booking, at the cost of touching potentially all n flights per booking.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n times bookings.length) in the worst case.
Space: O(n) for the result array.
Limitation: exactly like Range Addition, touching every flight in a booking's range is unnecessary; only the range's two boundaries actually change the "rate" of accumulation.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text:
Why touching every flight is wasteful: a booking only changes behavior at exactly two points, where it starts, and right after where it ends.

What can represent that instead: a difference array, where diff[first minus 1] += seats records the reservation beginning, and diff[last] -= seats records it ending, right after the last flight in range.

How is the true totals array recovered: one left-to-right running sum over the difference array, exactly as in Range Addition.

The core idea: mark each booking's two boundaries in O(1), then recover every flight's total with a single final prefix-sum sweep.

For every booking [first, last, seats], add seats to diff[first minus 1] and subtract seats from diff[last] in a difference array. Then sweep left to right, maintaining a running sum, assigning it as each flight's total seat count.

blocks.caption: Optimized flow: mark booking endpoints in O(1), reconstruct with one prefix-sum pass

codes.python:
def corp_flight_bookings(bookings, n):
    diff = [0] * (n + 1)
    for first, last, seats in bookings:
        diff[first - 1] += seats            # booking begins here (0-indexed)
        diff[last] -= seats                  # and ends right after 'last'

    result = [0] * n
    running = 0
    for i in range(n):
        running += diff[i]                    # one sweep reconstructs every flight's total
        result[i] = running
    return result

blocks.text: Marking +seats at first minus 1 and -seats at last means a running sum swept left to right includes seats at every flight from first to last (0-indexed), and stops including it right after. Since every booking's marks add together independently, one running sum over the combined difference array reconstructs every flight's true total in a single pass.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n plus bookings.length), O(1) per booking to mark, plus one linear sweep.
Space: O(n) for the difference array and result.

blocks.text: Corporate Flight Bookings is Range Addition wearing a different name: a range update per booking, applied efficiently with a difference array, then reconstructed once at the end with a prefix-sum sweep.

items: Mixing up the 1-indexed booking flight numbers with the 0-indexed output array, an off-by-one that shifts every seat count.
Placing the cancelling mark at last plus 1 in 1-indexed terms, which becomes just index "last" once converted to 0-indexed, easy to get backwards.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "does this remind you of another problem", think: this is Range Addition, just with flights and seat counts instead of a generic array and increments.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: The brute force runs in O(n times bookings.length) time; the optimized difference array approach runs in O(n plus bookings.length) time. Both use O(n) space.

items: Pattern: the difference array technique, identical to Range Addition, applied to flight seat bookings.
Core Idea: mark each booking's two boundaries in O(1), then reconstruct every flight's total seat count with one prefix-sum sweep.
Time: O(n times bookings.length) for the brute force, O(n plus bookings.length) for the optimized approach.
Most Important Observation: this is exactly Range Addition, just carefully converting between 1-indexed flights and a 0-indexed output array.
Interview Difficulty: straightforward once recognized as Range Addition in disguise.
One line memory trick: mark the booking's start and just-past-its-end, then one prefix sum tallies every flight.
